newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends day firmer, aluminium slumps.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends day firmer, aluminium slumps.

text.p: Copper got a modest burst of strength on Monday afternoon, regaining a foothold above $1,950 and propping up other metal prices.
Three month prices finished the afternoon kerb just above the much-watched $1,950 level, but failed to re-challenge the morning high of $1,965. Last business was at $1,951, up $11.
The market was wary about Tuesday's LME inventory data after a surprise fall of 19,125 tonnes of copper on Friday.
Some floor traders said there was talk of a 10,000-15,000-tonne fall in stocks but others said those figures sounded a bit high.
"In any case volumes have been down and the market cannot stay above $1,970. No one has any confidence above there," one floor trader said.
The upturn in copper helped lift most of the other metals into positive territory, except aluminium, which lost more ground.
Aluminium scored a second session of losses after several days last week of steaming to a high of $1,376.
Monday saw a steady erosion of values but they ended off their low of $1,346 at $1,352, down $7.50.
Lead popped higher after retesting Friday's 8-1/2 month low of $715 during the morning. Last kerb business was $725, up $6. Resistance was seen at $734.
Nickel closed the day marginally higher but well within recent ranges and below the $7,110 barrier. It finished at $7,070, up $15.
Tin ended barely changed at $5,980, up $5, and zinc closed firmer, probing resistance, at $1,024, also up $5.
Alloy was last quoted at $1,225/30, down from $1,230/35.
